title: The (n-2,2)-Spectrum of a Graph
summary: We study a representation-theoretic refinement of the ordinary Laplacian spectrum of a graph. Given a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, one may associate to it the element \[ X_G=\sum_{ij\in E(G)} (ij)\in \C[S_n]. \] The action of $X_G$ in irreducible representations of $S_n$ produces spectral invariants of graphs. The standard representation $(n-1,1)$ recovers the ordinary graph Laplacian spectrum, up to the elementary affine change $X_G=mI-L_G$, where $m=|E(G)|$. The next component, $(n-2,2)$, gives the first representation-theoretic correction. We give an explicit edge-space model for this…
